notes: This dataset tracks inexpensive NVIDIA Maxwell/Pascal GPUs that can still be useful for local LLM inference when acquisition cost or unusual form factor matters more than current-generation software longevity.

NVIDIA states that Maxwell and Pascal are feature-complete: CUDA Toolkit 12.x can still target them, while CUDA Toolkit 13.x removed offline compilation and library support. Runtime/framework compatibility therefore needs to be pinned and tested rather than assumed.
Marketplace prices are point-in-time observations. Model-fit guidance is approximate and depends on quantization, context/KV cache, runtime overhead, and whether model weights are fully GPU-resident.

software: llama.cpp CUDA when built for sm_61
hardware.software_lifecycle: Legacy. NVIDIA CUDA 13.x removed offline compilation and library support for Pascal; CUDA 12.x is the practical ceiling for building new Pascal-targeted binaries.
hardware.model_size_practicality: Approximate: best suited to small 3B-7B quantized models, embeddings, rerankers and auxiliary inference. 8GB VRAM leaves limited room for long context/KV cache or larger dense models.
quantization_compatibility: GGUF k-quants through compatible llama.cpp CUDA builds
Do not assume modern FP8/BF16 or CUDA-13-only kernels are available
hardware.llm_inference_suitability: Moderate for tiny low-cost nodes. The main appeal is CA$100-class used pricing and 75W slot-powered operation, not software longevity or large-model capacity.
physical_constraints: Low-profile server card; bracket/chassis compatibility should be checked
hardware.off_grid_notes: 75W board power and no auxiliary connector are attractive for constrained systems, but required blower/fan airflow adds system power and noise.

pricing.note: Toronto listing advertised CA$115 with both low-profile and full-height brackets; local classifieds can disappear quickly.

hardware.form_factor: 4.4 in high x 10.5 in long, dual-slot, full-height
software: llama.cpp CUDA when built for sm_52
hardware.software_lifecycle: Legacy/feature-complete. Maxwell offline compilation and library support were removed from CUDA Toolkit 13.x; use CUDA 12.x-era stacks and verify exact framework support.
hardware.model_size_practicality: Approximate: 24GB VRAM is enough for many 20B-35B-class models at aggressive 4-5 bit quantization if KV cache/context overhead fits. Throughput is limited by 288GB/s bandwidth and the old architecture.
quantization_compatibility: GGUF k-quants through compatible llama.cpp CUDA builds
FP32/FP16 execution supported by legacy CUDA paths
No Tensor Cores; modern low-precision kernels may not support Maxwell
hardware.llm_inference_suitability: Interesting only when extremely cheap. Its 24GB capacity can make models fit that cannot fit on newer 8-16GB cards, but power, cooling, bandwidth, and software age all work against it.
physical_constraints: Passive cooler requires high directed airflow
hardware.off_grid_notes: Low purchase cost does not translate to low operating cost: 250W board power plus forced server airflow makes sustained battery/solar use unattractive.

pricing.note: Representative pre-owned 24GB M40 listing around CA$203.68 with free shipping; marketplace condition, seller quality, duties and shipping vary.

hardware.form_factor: 4.4 in high x 10.5 in long, dual-slot, full-height
software: llama.cpp CUDA when built for sm_61
hardware.software_lifecycle: Legacy. Pascal can still be targeted with CUDA Toolkit 12.x, while CUDA Toolkit 13.x removed offline compilation and library support for Pascal.
hardware.model_size_practicality: Approximate: similar 24GB capacity envelope to Tesla M40, but 432GB/s bandwidth and active cooling make it substantially easier to use in a normal workstation. Many 20B-35B-class 4-5 bit models can fit if context/KV cache overhead is controlled.
quantization_compatibility: GGUF k-quants through compatible llama.cpp CUDA builds
INT8/FP16 support depends on legacy framework kernels
No Tensor Cores; CUDA-13-only and newer low-precision kernels should not be assumed
hardware.llm_inference_suitability: Moderate when found cheaply. More practical than passive Tesla M40 because it is actively cooled and faster, but it still carries a 250W load and Pascal software ceiling.
physical_constraints: Requires an auxiliary PCIe power connector
Used workstation cards may have unknown fan/bearing history
hardware.off_grid_notes: Active cooling helps integration, but 250W board power and only moderate bandwidth-per-watt make it a poor always-on solar choice.

pricing.note: Calgary local listing at CA$700 for a working workstation pull. Recent eBay.ca listings around CA$560-700 suggest this is plausible but not uniquely cheap.
